subject.title: [Feature Request] Code Verification and Signature for Skills

question: What trust model should OpenClaw enforce for SKILL.md skills before prompt loading and capability use?
rationale: The implementation choice affects trust roots, publisher keys, revocation, unsigned-skill compatibility, capability enforcement, and ClawHub policy, so automation cannot choose it safely from source inspection alone.

options.title: Design canonical signed-skill model
options.body: Define publisher or registry signatures, persisted expected content, runtime reverify, status surfaces, revocation behavior, and an unsigned migration policy before implementation.

options.title: Keep verification advisory for now
options.body: Treat current ClawHub verification and local hashes as operator information only, leaving runtime loading and capabilities unchanged until a broader security profile lands.

options.title: Enforce unsigned restrictions immediately
options.body: Require verified signatures for full capability access and degrade or reject unsigned skills with explicit upgrade and override behavior.

recommendation.title: Design canonical signed-skill model
recommendation.body: Define publisher or registry signatures, persisted expected content, runtime reverify, status surfaces, revocation behavior, and an unsigned migration policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest visible owner for both the native ClawHub skill path and the prior security-product review of this issue.
